articles.title: FERS September 2026 Payment: What day will federal retirees get paid next month?
articles.standfirst: OPM’s payment rules make the next deposit simple, but several calendar changes are coming later in 2026
articles.summary: OPM’s payment rules make the next deposit simple, but several calendar changes are coming later in 2026
articles.body:
Federal retirees planning their September finances have a straightforward payment date to work with this time, as the calendar will not force the next FERS annuity deposit to move because of a weekend or federal holiday.

The next regular Federal Employees Retirement System payment is scheduled to arrive on Tuesday, September 1, 2026.

That deposit represents the annuity earned during August rather than September itself, an important distinction that can sometimes cause confusion when federal retirees check payment calendars.

The Office of Personnel Management pays regular retirement annuities after the month in which the benefit accrues. As OPM explains, payments are made “usually on the first business day of the month.”

Since September 1 falls on a Tuesday in 2026, the normal schedule remains intact.

Retirees receiving their annuity through direct deposit should expect payment on that date, although individual banks and credit unions may differ in exactly when a deposit becomes visible in an account.

When will FERS retirees be paid in September 2026?

The September 1 deposit covers benefits accrued during August 2026.

Retirees looking further ahead should expect the annuity covering September to be paid on Thursday, October 1.

The following schedule shows the benefit month and scheduled payment date.

August 2026 = September 1, 2026

September 2026 = October 1, 2026

October 2026 = November 2, 2026

November 2026 = December 1, 2026

December 2026 = January 4, 2027

Calendar adjustments become important later in the year.

November 1 falls on a Sunday, meaning the October annuity moves to Monday, November 2. The payment covering December will also be delayed until Monday, January 4, 2027, because New Year’s Day is a federal holiday followed by a weekend.

What federal retirees should do if payment is missing

Most federal retirees and survivors receive their benefits through direct deposit, but a payment that does not appear as expected does not necessarily mean OPM has failed to issue it.

OPM advises retirees who have not received an expected payment to contact their financial institution first. Banks can sometimes provide information about deposits that are pending or still being processed.

If the payment remains missing, retirees can report the issue to OPM.

Federal annuitants can also use OPM’s online retirement services to manage aspects of their benefits, including direct-deposit information, tax withholding and certain financial allotments.

The most important date for the immediate payment cycle remains Tuesday, September 1, 2026. With no holiday or weekend disrupting the calendar, FERS retirees should see their August annuity arrive on the standard first-business-day schedule.

articles.title: Costco mini pain au chocolat: How good is the new pastry, where is available and how much it costs?
articles.standfirst: The latest Kirkland Signature bakery launch combines all-butter croissant dough, chocolate and a surprisingly low price
articles.summary: The latest Kirkland Signature bakery launch combines all-butter croissant dough, chocolate and a surprisingly low price
articles.body:
C ostco 's new Kirkland Signature Mini Pain au Chocolat comes in a 20-count package priced at $9.99, putting each pastry at roughly 50 cents.

Made with all-butter croissant dough and a chocolate filling, the bite-size pastries are baked fresh in Costco’s bakery department and are designed to deliver the same flaky, rich experience as a traditional pain au chocolat in a smaller format.

That combination of price and convenience is likely to be the biggest draw. Buying a chocolate croissant individually from a bakery or coffee shop can cost several dollars, while Costco’s version offers enough for a family breakfast, weekend brunch or several days of snacks for under $10.

An early review from Costco -focused social media account @costcobffs was positive, giving the new item a four-out-of-five rating and describing it simply as “Pretty good!”

How good is Costco’s Mini Pain au Chocolat?

The appeal starts with the basics. Each pastry uses all-butter croissant dough wrapped around chocolate, giving shoppers the familiar contrast of crisp, layered pastry and a sweet center. The smaller size also makes them easier to serve in different ways than a full-size croissant.

A couple can be paired with coffee in the morning, added to a brunch platter or served alongside fruit for a quick dessert. They can also be warmed before serving, which should help restore some of the crispness and softness associated with freshly baked pastry.

The value becomes even clearer when the package is broken down by serving. At $9.99 for 20, the cost is just under 50 cents per piece.

Households unlikely to finish the entire package quickly can freeze part of the batch and reheat individual portions later, helping extend their shelf life.

Where is Costco’s new pastry available?

Availability may be the only frustrating part. The Mini Pain au Chocolat has been spotted in Costco bakery departments in the United States, but bakery inventory can differ significantly between warehouses. A product appearing at one location does not necessarily mean it has reached every Costco nationwide.

Pricing can also vary slightly by location, meaning the reported $9.99 price should be viewed as the current observed price rather than a guaranteed nationwide figure.

Shoppers hoping to track it down can look for item number 2062190 at their local warehouse or ask bakery staff whether it is currently stocked.

Costco regularly rotates seasonal and new bakery products, which means popular launches can also disappear or sell out quickly.

The early impression, though, is straightforward. Costco isn't trying to reinvent pain au chocolat. It is offering a familiar bakery favorite in a smaller, cheaper format, and at around 50 cents each, the new pastries may be difficult to walk past if they show up at your local warehouse.

articles.title: Great white shark slams into kayak, sends fisherman into the ocean in terrifying encounter
articles.standfirst: One of the most dramatic examples of how quickly conditions can change when fishing
articles.summary: The footage is one of the most dramatic examples of how quickly conditions can change
articles.body:
Kayak fishing represents one of the purest forms of the sport. There is no engine, no large vessel, and often no barrier between the fisherman and the environment around him. That closeness to nature is part of the appeal

It is also part of the risk. A recent viral video captured a stark reminder of those dangers when a great white shark collided with a kayak, sending a fisherman into the ocean during a heart-stopping encounter that could have ended far differently.

Fortunately, the angler escaped unharmed. But the footage has quickly become one of the most dramatic examples of how quickly conditions can change when fishing in waters inhabited by some of the ocean's most powerful predators.

A routine fishing trip turns into chaos

The incident began like countless other offshore fishing trips. The kayaker had cameras mounted on his vessel and was actively fishing when he hooked a fish. As he worked to reel it in, excitement quickly turned to concern after he realized a large shark was pursuing the catch. The predator appeared to be tracking the struggling fish directly toward the kayak.

As the shark closed the distance, the fisherman could be heard reacting to the developing situation. Moments later, the massive animal surged forward and struck the rear of the kayak with tremendous force. The impact flipped the vessel and launched the angler into the water. For a few tense moments, the fisherman found himself sharing the ocean with a great white shark that had just overturned his craft.

Demonstrating remarkable composure under pressure, he immediately righted the kayak and climbed back aboard before the situation could escalate further. The video ends with the angler shaken but safe, having survived an encounter that many offshore fishermen hope never to experience.

The unique risks of kayak fishing

Kayak fishing has exploded in popularity across the United States over the past decade. The sport offers anglers access to waters that larger boats often cannot reach while providing an intimate connection with the environment. That accessibility comes with tradeoffs.

Unlike fishermen aboard larger vessels, kayakers are far more exposed to weather conditions, waves, currents, and wildlife. Whether it is navigating rough seas, battling large game fish, or encountering marine predators, anglers in kayaks operate with a much smaller margin for error. Those challenges become even more pronounced in ocean environments.

From giant halibut off Alaska's coast to marlin capable of towing kayaks for miles, offshore anglers routinely test themselves against some of nature's most powerful creatures. Encounters with sharks, however, remain among the most unnerving possibilities.

Despite the frightening nature of the video, marine experts emphasize that great white sharks are not actively hunting humans. Great whites are apex predators that can exceed 20 feet in length and weigh more than 4,000 pounds. Their primary prey includes seals, sea lions, and other marine mammals. Equipped with powerful senses, they can detect vibrations, movement, and even electrical signals in the water.

articles.title: A couple boarded a flight to Las Vegas and ended up getting married 35,000 feet in the air
articles.standfirst: What was supposed to be a private wedding turned into an unexpected celebration in front of 178 passengers.
articles.summary: What was supposed to be a private wedding turned into an unexpected celebration in front of 178 passengers.
articles.body:
Without a doubt, every couple decides where and how they want to get married, but there are moments that simply cannot be planned. That is exactly what happened to Sara Arroyo Montalvo and her partner, who boarded a flight to Las Vegas intending to reach the city and celebrate their wedding there . However, before the plane touched down, their trip took a completely different turn.

They got married in the sky

While the plane was flying at around 35,000 feet, the idea of a private wedding was left behind . The flight crew learned about the couple's plans and decided to surprise them with the opportunity to celebrate their wedding right there.

But how could they make it happen?

The flight's captain was also an ordained minister, so he was the one who officiated the ceremony.

Standing before them were the 178 passengers on the flight, who ended up becoming witnesses to a moment that had not originally been part of the celebration . The plane went from simply being their way of getting to Las Vegas to becoming the setting for their wedding.

For Montalvo, the coincidence was hard to ignore. In her post, she shared that the trip had another special detail: it was the first time the couple had flown with Southwest Airlines, meaning their debut with the airline came with a memory they will hardly ever forget.

And what about the wedding dress?

If the ceremony was unexpected, the details could not be conventional either. Without the usual elements of a wedding on hand, the flight attendants had to use whatever they had available aboard the plane to create the bride's look .

The result was a single-layer wedding dress made from toilet paper, paired with a veil made from the same material. To complete the look, the crew also created a bouquet using Southwest coffee stirrers.

Rather than taking away from the significance of the moment , those details turned it into a celebration that was completely different from what the couple had imagined.

articles.title: September 2026 Refund Payments: All deposits you may get next month
articles.standfirst: IRS tax refunds will continue arriving in September, but payment dates depend on when and how each return was filed.
articles.summary: IRS tax refunds will continue arriving in September, but payment dates depend on when and how each return was filed.
articles.body:
Americans still waiting for money from the IRS could receive their tax refund during September 2026 , even though the main filing season ended months ago.

There isn't one nationwide September refund payment date . Instead, deposits are issued as individual tax returns are processed and approved, meaning the timing will vary considerably between taxpayers.

The average federal refund is currently around $3,268, according to the latest IRS data cited by Kiplinger, although individual payments can be significantly higher or lower.

Which IRS refunds could arrive in September?

Taxpayers who electronically filed a return and selected direct deposit generally receive their refund within 21 days after the IRS accepts the return.

That means someone whose return is accepted during the first part of September could potentially receive their payment before the month ends.

Mailed returns take considerably longer, generally around four to eight weeks to process. Errors, additional reviews, claimed tax credits or outstanding debts owed to the IRS can also delay a refund.

The IRS has largely moved away from paper refund checks for individual taxpayers in 2026, making electronic payments the standard option in most cases.

Taxpayers can follow their payment using the IRS Where's My Refund? service, which can normally begin displaying information within 24 hours of an electronically filed return being accepted.

Are tariff refunds coming to consumers in September?

Recent headlines about tariff refunds may also cause confusion, but these shouldn't be mistaken for a new federal payment program for households.

Some companies have received substantial refunds connected to tariffs paid on imported goods. Those payments go to businesses that directly paid the import taxes rather than automatically being distributed to consumers.

There is therefore no confirmed nationwide September tariff refund check or direct deposit available to every American based on the reporting currently available.

For most individuals expecting a refund next month, the relevant payment will be a federal or state income tax refund that is already being processed.

State refund schedules vary separately, so taxpayers waiting for state money should check directly with their state's tax or revenue department.

September payments will ultimately depend on filing date, processing status and the method chosen to receive the refund.

articles.title: Donald Trump's secret privilege for Natalie Harp at Mar-a-Lago comes to light, fueling new rumors
articles.standfirst: Harp’s reported privilege at Trump’s golf club has fueled wider questions about her growing influence around the president
articles.summary: Harp’s reported privilege at Trump’s golf club has fueled wider questions about her growing influence around the president
articles.body:
Donald Trump’s campaign staffers reportedly had their eyes on one particularly lavish perk at his Palm Beach-area golf club: a Sunday buffet featuring an extravagant spread that included whole lobsters, ham, omelets and fresh fruit.

But there was a catch. According to author Michael Wolff , most staffers weren’t allowed to enjoy it. Natalie Harp, however, was reportedly treated differently.

Speaking on the Inside Trump’s Head podcast, Wolff claimed Harp was “always allowed” into the exclusive buffet, and not only for herself.

He said she regularly arrived with her mother on Sundays, a practice that allegedly left other members of Trump’s team questioning why she received such access.

Wolff described the buffet as a throwback to an era of extravagant American dining, saying the spread was so impressive that staffers would talk about it despite being unable to participate.

He claimed some became visibly emotional when discussing the food, particularly the opportunity to take a whole lobster and return for another serving.

The unusual arrangement allegedly became a source of conversation among campaign employees and even the club’s staff. Wolff said workers wondered whether Harp was actually authorized to attend, particularly because she reportedly told them Trump himself had given her permission.

Harp’s growing influence has attracted attention

Harp , now 35, joined Trump’s communications operation in 2022 and quickly became a familiar presence around him. She earned the nickname “the human printer” because she often carried a portable printer and provided Trump with printed news stories, social-media posts and other information.

Wolff has previously claimed that Trump’s staff became increasingly concerned about Harp’s influence. According to the author, employees worried that she was gaining greater access to the then-candidate and playing an expanding role in shaping the information and opinions reaching him.

Her proximity to Trump has remained evident since his return to the White House. In July, Harp was reportedly among a small group of aides who accompanied Trump aboard a secondary aircraft after a security threat prompted an unusual departure from a Turkish airport.

Other members of the group included Dan Scavino and Walt Nauta.

Questions have also been raised about Harp’s security clearance. Reporting has indicated that she worked in the White House for more than a year without obtaining the routine clearance generally expected of West Wing employees, prompting concerns about what information she may have encountered.

The White House has defended Harp , with spokesman Davis Ingle describing her as one of Trump’s most loyal and hardworking aides. Ingle has also strongly criticized Wolff, dismissing his claims and attacking his credibility.

articles.title: Delaying Social Security benefits: How the strategy works and the maximum you can receive
articles.standfirst: Waiting until age 70 can significantly increase monthly Social Security income.
articles.summary: Waiting until age 70 can significantly increase monthly Social Security income.
articles.body:
Delaying Social Security benefits can provide retirees with a substantially larger monthly payment, but the strategy depends on being able to cover living expenses while waiting to claim.

Benefits generally increase by about 8 percent for every year a person delays claiming beyond full retirement age, up to age 70.

Serving Those Who Serve describes the tradeoff clearly: “Delaying Social Security past full retirement age (FRA) increases your benefit through delayed retirement credits – generally about 8% per year up to age 70.”

The challenge is funding the years before those larger payments begin.

How delaying Social Security benefits works

CNBC reports that waiting can also increase the value retirees receive from future cost of living adjustments.

“You need to protect yourself against living a long life, and you don't want to have regret,” financial planner James Mahaney said. “Social Security is your best tool to get there.”

Someone eligible for $3,000 per month at full retirement age could receive an estimated $3,960 at 70 before COLAs, according to the example cited by CNBC.

Once historical COLAs were included in Mahaney's example, that age 70 benefit increased to $5,091, compared with $3,205 at full retirement age and $2,250 at 62.

“Having a built-in cost-of-living protection is one of the central things that makes Social Security unique,” financial planner Joe Elsasser said.

His advice for people worried about waiting is straightforward: “Don't act out of fear. Model it.”

How much can delaying increase your benefits?

The strategy can produce a significant difference over retirement.

CNBC's example found that waiting from 62 until 70 produced an approximate 76 percent total increase, with larger future COLAs because those adjustments are applied to a higher benefit.

But delaying isn't automatically the right decision for everyone.

Serving Those Who Serve warns that people must first determine whether pensions, savings or other income can comfortably cover the gap years.

“If covering that gap means pulling too much from your portfolio or stretching your cash flow, it may not be worth it.”

The strategy can be particularly valuable for married couples because delaying the higher earner's benefit may also increase what a surviving spouse eventually receives.

And the decision doesn't have to be made eight years in advance.

“It's not an irrevocable decision at 62 to delay to 70,” Mahaney said. “Maybe look at it each year.”

articles.title: 80% VA disability benefits: How hard is it to go from 80% to 100%?
articles.standfirst: Moving from an 80% VA rating to 100% can be difficult because disability percentages aren't simply added together.
articles.summary: Moving from an 80% VA rating to 100% can be difficult because disability percentages aren't simply added together.
articles.body:
Veterans rated at 80% disability may receive significantly more compensation if they reach the 100% level, but getting there isn't as straightforward as adding another 20% rating.

In 2026, a veteran with no dependents receives $2,102.15 per month at 80%, compared with $3,938.58 at 100%. That is a difference of $1,836.43 each month.

The difficulty comes from the way the Department of Veterans Affairs combines multiple disabilities.

Why going from 80% to 100% VA disability is difficult

CCK Law explains that reaching a schedular 100% rating from 80% can require substantial additional disability.

“It’s important to note that the way VA calculates veterans’ overall combined rating is not simply to add each disability together. Instead, they use a special algorithm and formula to do so,” CCK Law partner Michael Lostritto said.

According to CCK Law, someone at a schedular 80% rating would generally need another condition rated at 80%, or several additional disabilities combining to the equivalent, to reach a combined schedular 100%.

Veterans can potentially seek an increased rating if an existing service-connected condition has worsened, appeal an earlier VA decision, or file claims for qualifying secondary conditions.

“It’s really important to bolster your claim or appeal with lay evidence or medical evidence in order to substantiate that an increased rating is warranted. It’s also very important - it’s critical - to attend your C&P exams,” Lostritto said.

TDIU can provide another route to 100% benefits

Some veterans may instead qualify for Total Disability based on Individual Unemployability, known as TDIU.

TDIU can pay compensation at the 100% rate even when a veteran's combined schedular rating remains below 100%.

“TDIU requires you to show that your service-connected disabilities prevent you from gaining and maintaining substantially gainful employment,” Lostritto said. “It allows veterans to be compensated at the 100 percent level, despite the fact that they’re otherwise not combined at the 100 percent rate.”

For schedular TDIU, CCK Law says a veteran generally needs one service-connected disability rated at 60% or higher, or multiple disabilities with at least one rated at 40% and a combined rating of at least 70%.

So while moving directly from 80% to schedular 100% can be challenging, worsening conditions, secondary claims, appeals or TDIU may provide alternative paths depending on the veteran's circumstances.

articles.title: Tariff Refunds 2026: Which businesses are eligible to get refunds?
articles.standfirst: Billions returning to importers after the tariff ruling.
articles.summary: Billions returning to importers after the tariff ruling.
articles.body:
Thousands of U.S. businesses are receiving tariff refunds in 2026 after the Supreme Court struck down many of the tariffs collected under emergency powers.

The key requirement is straightforward: refunds generally go to the importers that directly paid the affected tariff charges to the federal government.

That means retailers, manufacturers, small businesses and shipping companies may qualify if they were the importer of record and paid tariffs that were later invalidated.

Consumers who indirectly covered those costs through higher prices normally aren't entitled to claim money directly from the government.

Which businesses are eligible for tariff refunds?

The refunds are being returned primarily to companies and importers that actually paid the tariff fees.

Major businesses have already received enormous sums. Walmart has received approximately $2.9 billion, while Apple has received about $2.2 billion. Target and Nike have each recovered close to $1 billion.

Small businesses that directly imported goods and paid the affected tariffs may also be eligible, although the financial impact on them has often been more severe.

Sara Albrecht , chairman and CEO of the Liberty Justice Center, explained how much pressure the tariffs placed on smaller companies.

“They basically loaned all of their working capital to the government for the past year,” Albrecht said.

Even receiving the original tariff money back doesn't necessarily undo the financial damage.

“There's so many opportunities, costs that came along with this. They couldn't hire people, they couldn't buy machinery, they couldn't invest in new products or new supply chains. Getting back their money and passing it on to customers in a perfect world would be great, but it's not really a straight pass through for small businesses,” she added.

Will customers receive any tariff refund money?

Consumers generally won't receive federal tariff refund checks because they weren't the parties that directly paid Customs.

“It’s all just a giant transfer from consumers to corporations,” said Michael Ettlinger , a senior fellow at the Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy. “You can’t really design a worse tax than that.”

Shipping companies are an important exception.

UPS, FedEx and DHL have pledged to return qualifying tariff refunds to customers because those companies often billed importers directly for the exact tariff amount.

“Now that FedEx and UPS have received a refund of that $100 from the federal government, they are absolutely obligated to return it to the person they collected it from,” Syracuse University law dean Terence Lau said.

Retailers face a different situation because tariffs were often absorbed into general prices rather than separately charged.

“It’s like the retailer stirred the tax into the batter,” Lau said. “So once it’s cooked into the cake you can’t just back it out ingredient by ingredient anymore because it’s not separated.”

articles.standfirst: Why investigators still believe Nancy Guthrie’s case could be solved
articles.summary: Why investigators still believe Nancy Guthrie’s case could be solved
articles.body:
Nearly seven months after Nancy Guthrie disappeared from her Tucson, Arizona, home, investigators are still working to determine what happened to the 84-year-old mother of Today anchor Savannah Guthrie.

Despite the length of the investigation, the case hasn't been classified as a cold case, and authorities continue to pursue several potentially important leads.

Nancy was reported missing on February 1 after she failed to attend a virtual church service. Her disappearance quickly attracted national attention, with investigators eventually treating the case as an apparent abduction.

A $1 million reward remains available for information that could help authorities locate Nancy or lead to a breakthrough.

NewsNation senior national correspondent Brian Entin , who's followed the investigation closely, says the level of resources devoted to the case is unusual.

According to Entin , FBI agents and local detectives remain assigned to Nancy's disappearance as their full-time responsibility. Investigators are also meeting regularly, allowing new information and evidence to be assessed as it emerges.

That continued commitment is one reason Entin remains optimistic that the mystery could eventually be solved. He has also pointed to advances in forensic technology, particularly DNA testing, as a potential game changer.

“I really still feel that there’s going to be a resolution and that [detectives are] going to solve it. I just know through my sources how many people are working behind the scenes,” he told Us magazine.

DNA evidence recovered inside Nancy's home is among the most closely watched pieces of evidence. Investigators have been working to analyze biological material that could potentially reveal another person's involvement.

While some testing hasn't produced a usable profile, forensic science continues to advance, meaning evidence that can't be fully interpreted today could potentially provide answers in the future.

The clues that could eventually crack the case

Surveillance footage is another significant element of the investigation. Video captured around Nancy's home showed a masked individual near a doorbell camera around the time she vanished.

Establishing who that person was, how they reached the property and where they went afterward could help investigators build a more complete timeline.

Authorities have also released ransom communications connected to the case. One message reportedly demanded millions of dollars in cryptocurrency, while another claimed Nancy had died and provided information about where her body had supposedly been left. Investigators haven't publicly identified a suspect or person of interest.

The discovery of human remains in the Tucson desert has also sparked speculation because of the proximity to Nancy's home.

However, authorities said there was no indication the remains belonged to her, and investigators later determined they weren't connected to her disappearance.

Such discoveries aren't unusual in southern Arizona. The harsh Sonoran Desert is vast, and extreme heat, flash flooding, animals and difficult terrain can make both searches and identification exceptionally challenging.

Pima County receives numerous sets of unidentified remains each year, many believed to involve people who died while attempting to cross the border.

Until authorities determine what happened, Nancy's disappearance remains an active investigation, and one new clue could still provide the answer her family has been waiting for.

articles.title: What is the SSDI payment schedule for September 2026? Dates for next month's benefits
articles.standfirst: Four September payment dates depending on eligibility and birthday.
articles.summary: Four September payment dates depending on eligibility and birthday.
articles.body:
Social Security Disability Insurance recipients will receive their September 2026 payments on different dates depending on when they first began receiving benefits and, for most beneficiaries, their date of birth.

The Social Security Administration's official 2026 calendar confirms four relevant Social Security payment dates during September: September 3, 9, 16 and 23.

Most SSDI recipients will be paid on one of the three Wednesdays during the month, while people who began receiving Social Security benefits before May 1997 follow a different schedule.

When will SSDI be paid in September 2026?

Recipients who started receiving Social Security before May 1997 are scheduled to receive their September benefit on Thursday, September 3.

The same September 3 Social Security payment date applies to people who receive both Social Security and Supplemental Security Income. Their SSI payment is issued separately on September 1.

Everyone else generally follows the SSA's birthday-based Wednesday schedule.

People born between the 1st and 10th of any month will receive their September SSDI payment on Wednesday, September 9.

Those with birthdays from the 11th through the 20th are scheduled for Wednesday, September 16, while beneficiaries born between the 21st and 31st will be paid on Wednesday, September 23.

How does the SSDI payment schedule work?

The SSA normally distributes Social Security benefits according to the beneficiary's birth date.

Its official calendar states that benefits for birthdays from the "1st - 10th" are paid on the second Wednesday, those from the "11th - 20th" on the third Wednesday and birthdays from the "21st - 31st" on the fourth Wednesday.

That system applies to SSDI as well as most other Social Security benefits unless the recipient falls under one of the earlier payment rules.

The SSA also advises beneficiaries not to immediately assume there is a problem when a payment doesn't arrive on its scheduled date.

Its calendar says recipients should "allow three additional mailing days before contacting Social Security" if the expected payment hasn't arrived.

That means September SSDI recipients should first identify which payment group applies to them before determining exactly when their next deposit is due.

articles.title: Student loans for bad credit: How can you get one with a poor credit score?
articles.standfirst: Federal loans may still be available even with weak credit.
articles.summary: Federal loans may still be available even with weak credit.
articles.body:
Having bad credit doesn't automatically prevent you from getting a student loan , although the options available can look very different depending on whether you apply for federal or private borrowing.

Experian defines bad credit as typically a FICO score of 579 or below, while Citizens notes that scores between 580 and 669 are generally considered fair.

Experian's guidance is reassuring for borrowers worried that a low score has closed the door completely.

"Yes, you can get student loans with bad credit. Federal student loans don't have a minimum credit score and most don't require a credit check at all."

Federal student loans can be easier with bad credit

Federal borrowing is usually the first place to look because Direct Subsidized and Direct Unsubsidized Loans don't use your credit score when determining eligibility.

Citizens explains: "Your credit score has no impact on whether you qualify for federal student loans."

Borrowers apply by completing the FAFSA each year they attend college.

Parent PLUS loans work differently. They do require a credit check, although Citizens says the review focuses on adverse credit history such as missed payments, bankruptcy or foreclosure rather than simply requiring a high score.

Experian similarly notes that federal loans offer "standardized interest rates," meaning borrowers don't receive a higher rate simply because their credit score is weaker.

Private student loans are harder to get

Private loans normally involve much more scrutiny.

Citizens says most private lenders look for a score in the mid 600s, adding that "bad or no credit loans exist, but you'll typically have a higher interest rate."

A cosigner can therefore become important.

Experian says: "Because a cosigner agrees to repay the loan if you can't, their creditworthiness can not only help you get approved but also secure more favorable loan terms."

Citizens makes the same point, noting that borrowers with limited or poor credit will "most likely" need a cosigner who satisfies the lender's requirements.

Some lenders may look beyond credit scores and consider academic performance, future career prospects or progress through a degree program.

But Experian warns that private options aimed at borrowers without a cosigner "tend to be very costly ways to borrow."

Both sources therefore point toward the same strategy: use federal aid first, then consider private loans only if necessary, ideally with a strong cosigner and after comparing terms carefully.

articles.title: Social Security proposals in Congress: What changes could affect your SSI and SSDI benefits?
articles.standfirst: Several proposals could reshape payments, taxes and future program funding.
articles.summary: Several proposals could reshape payments, taxes and future program funding.
articles.body:
Congress is considering several Social Security proposals that could eventually affect millions of Americans receiving retirement, SSI or SSDI benefits , although none of the major changes discussed here have become law.

One of the most significant ideas is the Social Security Expansion Act , which would permanently raise monthly benefits by about $200, or roughly $2,400 a year.

The proposal would also change how Social Security is funded by applying taxes to income above $250,000, including certain investment income.

What could change for Social Security recipients?

Supporters argue that the extra $200 would provide a much larger increase than a typical annual cost of living adjustment.

The AOL report notes that the 2026 COLA of 2.8 percent increased the average monthly Social Security payment by only about $56.

Under the proposed legislation, the additional $200 would be permanent rather than tied to one year's inflation calculation.

The bill would also aim to extend Social Security's long-term solvency. Supporters say taxing income above $250,000 could help extend the trust fund by 75 years.

That matters because the Old Age and Survivors Insurance trust fund is currently projected to run short of reserves by the end of 2032. Without legislative action, incoming payroll taxes would cover only about 78 percent of scheduled benefits.

Could SSI and SSDI payments be affected?

Other proposals being debated in Congress could affect how disability and low-income benefits are calculated, although the exact impact would depend on which legislation, if any, eventually passes.

Any changes to benefit formulas, eligibility requirements or Social Security funding could potentially influence SSDI recipients because SSDI is financed through the Social Security system.

SSI works differently because it is needs-based, but congressional changes to benefit levels, eligibility rules or federal payment standards could still affect recipients.

The most important point is that these remain proposals.

The AOL report describes the Social Security Expansion Act as "a mere proposal, not law" and says its chances of passage are currently considered low.

That means recipients shouldn't change their budgets based on a possible $200 increase or any other proposed adjustment yet.

Until Congress passes legislation and it is signed into law, current SSI and SSDI payment rules remain in place.

articles.title: Powerball Winning Numbers: Results for Monday, August 31 drawing for the $131 million jackpot
articles.standfirst: The jackpot has climbed again after no grand prize winner on Saturday.
articles.summary: The jackpot has climbed again after no grand prize winner on Saturday.
articles.body:
Powerball players will have another chance to win big on Monday, August 31, with an estimated $131 million jackpot available in the latest drawing.

The winning numbers haven't yet been drawn . Monday's Powerball drawing will take place at 10:59 p.m. ET from the Florida Lottery draw studio in Tallahassee.

A winner choosing the cash option instead of the full annuity would receive an estimated $56.8 million before applicable federal and jurisdictional taxes.

What are the Powerball winning numbers for August 31?

The official winning numbers for Monday, August 31 will be confirmed after the 10:59 p.m. ET drawing.

Players need to match five white balls selected from numbers 1 through 69 and one red Powerball from 1 through 26 to win the jackpot.

The latest confirmed numbers came from the Saturday, August 29 drawing.

Those winning numbers were 18, 56, 62, 65 and 67, with Powerball 18. The Power Play multiplier was 2x.

Nobody matched all five white balls and the red Powerball, allowing the jackpot to increase from an estimated $119 million to $131 million.

There were also no Match 5 plus Power Play $2 million winners, although tickets sold in California and Georgia each matched all five white balls to win the $1 million prize.

When is the next Powerball drawing?

Monday's drawing begins at 10:59 p.m. ET , which is 9:59 p.m. CT, 8:59 p.m. MT and 7:59 p.m. PT.

Powerball drawings take place every Monday, Wednesday and Saturday.

Tickets normally cost $2 per play, although Idaho and Montana bundle Power Play with Powerball for a minimum $3 purchase. Sales cutoff times vary depending on the jurisdiction and can be one or two hours before the drawing.

The jackpot winner can choose between the advertised $131 million annuity, paid through 30 graduated payments over 29 years, or the $56.8 million lump sum cash option.

Monday's official winning numbers will only be known once the August 31 drawing has taken place.

articles.title: Has Melania been forgotten? Trump spends weekend at his golf club with trusted aide Natalie Harp
articles.standfirst: Critics are once again focusing on Harp’s access to the president, though allies insist their relationship is strictly professional
articles.summary: Critics are once again focusing on Harp’s access to the president, though allies insist their relationship is strictly professional
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump is once again facing questions over the optics surrounding his relationship with aide Natalie Harp after the two were photographed together during a weekend visit to his Virginia golf club.

Trump , 80, and Harp , 35, were seen seated in the back of a vehicle, with Harp smiling while looking at her phone.

First Lady Melania Trump wasn't pictured with them, and the image quickly became another flashpoint for critics who have already been closely watching Harp’s unusually prominent role around the president.

“What is wrong him, and HER?? That whole situation is so gross,” one person wrote on X. Another added: “He is a pathetic mess. And she is worse.”

There's no evidence of an improper relationship, but the reaction reflects the scrutiny Harp now attracts whenever she is seen in close proximity to Trump .

Her role inside the administration has become increasingly visible, and that visibility has fueled speculation online even as allies continue to insist that the relationship is entirely professional.

White House role keeps drawing attention

Harp works as a special assistant to the president and has long been one of the staffers with the closest access to Trump .

She has been associated with managing printed materials, helping with social-media posts and accompanying the president during travel and public events.

Rep. Anna Paulina Luna has publicly rejected suggestions that there is anything inappropriate about Harp’s position.

“She’s been nothing but professional and an absolute killer when it comes to getting her job done,” Luna said. “I would kill to have someone like her on my team.”

Luna has also described Harp ’s relationship with Trump as “100 percent professional.”

That hasn't stopped critics from focusing on the frequency with which Harp appears beside the president.

The scrutiny intensified after footage resurfaced showing Harp helping prepare Trump ’s social-media posts, adding to questions about how much influence she has over his day-to-day communications.

Selective public schedule adds to optics

Melania Trump ’s comparatively limited public appearances have added another layer to the attention.

The First Lady returned to the spotlight on August 20 for a White House initiative involving foster care youth, opening her remarks with a joke about her absence.

“I heard you missed me. Here I am,” she said.

Harp , meanwhile, has remained a regular presence at events involving the president.

She was also seen at the Freedom 250 Grand Prix in Washington, where she sat several rows behind Trump and Melania.

Critics have repeatedly tried to draw conclusions from those appearances, but Harp ’s supporters argue that the speculation is unfair.

“People can be very mean to successful, pretty women,” Luna said. “And that is what is happening to Natalie.”

The latest photo has now revived the debate once again. Nothing in the image establishes anything beyond a staffer traveling with the president, but Harp ’s access and Melania ’s limited visibility have ensured that the optics will continue to be dissected.
